Compression middleware Supports Brotli, Zstandard, and gzip (via libdeflate). Negotiates encoding from Accept-Encoding with quality values. Preference order (server tie-breaker): Zstandard > Brotli > gzip. Sensitive routes (CSRF/session data in HTML) can opt out per-request by setting res.compress = false in the handler to mitigate BREACH-style compression side channels.Returns the default per-request compression options with compression enabled for common safe methods.Returns the default app-wide compression policy options with the standard minimum size and level.Returns true if a Content-Encoding header indicates the response body is already compressed.Returns true if a Content-Type header indicates an already-compressed file format.Sets the app-wide compression policy; must be called before the server starts listening.Middleware that negotiates response compression from the Accept-Encoding header and marks the response for compressed output.

CompressionPolicyOptions = object
  enabled*: bool
  minBytes*: int
  minSavingsRatio*: float
  level*: int ## Accepted for API stability but currently a no-op: compression runs
              ## inline on the event loop with no backpressure gating. Do not rely on
              ## this to cap CPU under load.
  backpressureThresholdBytes*: int ## Accepted for API stability but currently a no-op: bodies are not
                                   ## offloaded to a worker thread; compression is synchronous.
  offloadThresholdBytes*: int

Sets app-wide compression policy. Must be called before listen(); the values are read without synchronization by the response path at request time, so mutating them after the server starts is a data race in multi-threaded/cluster mode.
